1	"""
     2	Price it: from the linked graph to copies at risk.
     3	
     4	For every edition still being packed: remaining = day-one demand - packed. For every part in
     5	its bill of materials: needed = remaining x quantity per copy. Usable stock = the latest book
     6	stock minus what the evidence says is not really there or can't be used (live linker issues with
     7	a stock effect). Gap = needed - usable. Everything comes from the data; nothing is typed in.
     8	"""
     9	
    10	import math
    11	import re
    12	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
    13	from datetime import datetime, timedelta
    14	
    15	import pandas as pd
    16	
    17	from ask_soony.verifier.impact.timing import lead_hours, parse_moment, runs_dry, shift_windows
    18	
    19	# Linker issues whose units are book stock that is not really usable
    20	STOCK_EFFECT_RULES = {
    21	    "delivery_vs_receipt": "booked but not delivered",
    22	    "failed_lot_in_stock": "failed inspection",
    23	    "remark_names_other_part": "wrong part booked",
    24	    "old_revision_in_stock": "old revision, must not be packed",
    25	}
    26	
    27	
    28	@dataclass
    29	class Deduction:
    30	    reason: str
    31	    units: float
    32	    issue: str  # record id of the issue's record
    33	    context: str
    34	
    35	
    36	@dataclass
    37	class PartNeed:
    38	    part: str
    39	    description: str | None
    40	    editions: list[str]
    41	    needed: float
    42	    book_stock: float
    43	    book_as_of: str | None
    44	    deductions: list[Deduction] = field(default_factory=list)
    45	    plan_status: str | None = None  # what the launch plan says ('ok', 'CHECK')
    46	    supply: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)  # options to close the gap
    47	    per_copy: dict[str, float] = field(default_factory=dict)  # edition → parts per copy
    48	    used_today: float | None = None
    49	    rate_per_hour: float | None = None  # how fast the lines use it
    50	    runs_dry: datetime | None = None  # None: lasts to the end of packing
    51	    fixes: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)  # supply that can arrive in time, with act-by
    52	
    53	    @property
    54	    def usable(self) -> float:
    55	        return max(self.book_stock - sum(d.units for d in self.deductions), 0)
    56	
    57	    @property
    58	    def gap(self) -> float:
    59	        return max(self.needed - self.usable, 0)
    60	
    61	    @property
    62	    def gap_if_acted(self) -> float:
    63	        """The gap left if every fix that can arrive in time is taken."""
    64	        closable = sum(f["quantity"] for f in self.fixes if f["in_time"])
    65	        return max(self.gap - closable, 0)
    66	
    67	
    68	@dataclass
    69	class Edition:
    70	    product: str
    71	    name: str | None
    72	    launch_date: str | None
    73	    day_one: float
    74	    packed: float
    75	    packed_as_of: str | None
    76	    rate_per_hour: float | None
    77	
    78	    @property
    79	    def remaining(self) -> float:
    80	        return max(self.day_one - self.packed, 0)
    81	
    82	
    83	@dataclass
    84	class Shortfall:
    85	    editions: list[Edition]
    86	    parts: list[PartNeed]
    87	    excluded: list[dict]  # BOM parts not stocked separately, with the evidence
    88	    now: datetime | None = None  # time of the newest stock figures
    89	    packing_ends: datetime | None = None
    90	    hours_left: float | None = None
    91	
    92	    def at_risk(self, product: str, acted: bool = False) -> tuple[float, str | None]:
    93	        """
    94	        Copies of an edition at risk from parts only it uses, and the part that binds.
    95	        acted=True: after every fix that can still arrive in time.
    96	        """
    97	
    98	        def gap(p: PartNeed) -> float:
    99	            return p.gap_if_acted if acted else p.gap
   100	
   101	        own = [p for p in self.parts if p.editions == [product] and gap(p) > 0]
   102	        if not own:
   103	            return 0, None
   104	        worst = max(own, key=gap)
   105	        return gap(worst), worst.part
   106	
   107	    @property
   108	    def shared_gaps(self) -> list[PartNeed]:
   109	        return [p for p in self.parts if len(p.editions) > 1 and p.gap > 0]
   110	
   111	
   112	def _latest(rows: list[dict]) -> dict | None:
   113	    """The newest record by as_of; records without a date come last."""
   114	    return max(rows, key=lambda r: r["as_of"] or "", default=None)
   115	
   116	
   117	def _known_parts(records: pd.DataFrame) -> set[str]:
   118	    return set(records[records.kind == "part"].material_id.dropna())
   119	
   120	
   121	def _fitted_parts(records: pd.DataFrame, known: set[str]) -> dict[str, dict]:
   122	    """
   123	    Parts a supplier says it fits into another part ('fitted by supplier into CMP-...'), so they
   124	    are never stocked on their own. Learned from the suppliers' own part lists.
   125	    """
   126	    fitted = {}
   127	    for r in records[records.kind == "supplier_part"].to_dict("records"):
   128	        note = r["attrs"].get("note") or ""
   129	        others = [p for p in known if p != r["material_id"] and re.search(re.escape(p), note)]
   130	        if others and re.search(r"fitted|included|built[- ]in|assembled", note, re.I):
   131	            fitted[r["material_id"]] = {
   132	                "inside": others[0],
   133	                "evidence": note,
   134	                "source": r["source"],
   135	            }
   136	    return fitted
   137	
   138	
   139	def compute(records: pd.DataFrame, issues: pd.DataFrame) -> Shortfall:
   140	    rows = records.to_dict("records")
   141	    by_kind: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
   142	    for r in rows:
   143	        by_kind.setdefault(r["kind"], []).append(r)
   144	
   145	    # Editions: launch products with a day-one demand
   146	    editions = []
   147	    for product in by_kind.get("product", []):
   148	        demand = product["attrs"].get("day_one_qty")
   149	        if not demand:
   150	            continue
   151	        pid = product["material_id"]
   152	        packed = _latest([r for r in by_kind.get("packed_count", []) if r["material_id"] == pid])
   153	        plans = [r for r in by_kind.get("plan_edition", []) if r["material_id"] == pid]
   154	        plan = _latest(plans)
   155	        packed_qty = (packed or {}).get("attrs", {}).get("quantity")
   156	        if packed_qty is None and plan:
   157	            packed_qty = plan["attrs"].get("packed")
   158	        rate = next(
   159	            (p["attrs"]["rate_per_hour"] for p in plans if p["attrs"].get("rate_per_hour")), None
   160	        )
   161	        editions.append(
   162	            Edition(
   163	                pid,
   164	                product["attrs"].get("name"),
   165	                product["attrs"].get("launch_date"),
   166	                demand,
   167	                packed_qty or 0,
   168	                (packed or plan or {}).get("as_of"),
   169	                rate,
   170	            )
   171	        )
   172	    remaining = {e.product: e.remaining for e in editions}
   173	
   174	    # Needs from the bill of materials
   175	    known = _known_parts(records)
   176	    fitted = _fitted_parts(records, known)
   177	    needs: dict[str, PartNeed] = {}
   178	    excluded = []
   179	    descriptions = {
   180	        r["material_id"]: r["attrs"].get("description") for r in by_kind.get("part", [])
   181	    }
   182	    for line in by_kind.get("bom_line", []):
   183	        parent, part = line["attrs"]["parent"], line["material_id"]
   184	        if parent not in remaining:
   185	            continue
   186	        if part in fitted:
   187	            excluded.append({"part": part, "edition": parent, **fitted[part]})
   188	            continue
   189	        need = needs.setdefault(part, PartNeed(part, descriptions.get(part), [], 0, 0, None))
   190	        need.editions.append(parent)
   191	        need.per_copy[parent] = line["attrs"].get("qty_per") or 1
   192	        need.needed += remaining[parent] * need.per_copy[parent]
   193	
   194	    # Book stock: the newest count per part; else the stock snapshot
   195	    for part, need in needs.items():
   196	        latest = _latest([r for r in by_kind.get("stock_count", []) if r["material_id"] == part])
   197	        if latest:
   198	            need.book_stock, need.book_as_of = latest["attrs"].get("quantity") or 0, latest["as_of"]
   199	            need.used_today = latest["attrs"].get("used_today")
   200	        else:
   201	            batches = [r for r in by_kind.get("stock_batch", []) if r["material_id"] == part]
   202	            need.book_stock = sum(r["attrs"].get("quantity") or 0 for r in batches)
   203	            need.book_as_of = _latest(batches)["as_of"] if batches else None
   204	        plan_part = _latest([r for r in by_kind.get("plan_part", []) if r["material_id"] == part])
   205	        need.plan_status = plan_part["attrs"].get("status") if plan_part else None
   206	
   207	    # Deductions: live issues with a stock effect
   208	    for issue in issues.to_dict("records"):
   209	        reason = STOCK_EFFECT_RULES.get(issue["rule"])
   210	        units = issue.get("units")
   211	        if (
   212	            not reason
   213	            or not issue.get("live")
   214	            or units is None
   215	            or (isinstance(units, float) and math.isnan(units))
   216	        ):
   217	            continue

   219	            needs[issue["material_id"]].deductions.append(
   220	                Deduction(reason, float(units), issue["record_id"], issue.get("context") or "")
   221	            )
   222	
   223	    # Supply that could close a gap before launch
   224	    launch = min((e.launch_date for e in editions if e.launch_date), default=None)
   225	    for plan in by_kind.get("plan_inbound", []):
   226	        need = needs.get(plan["material_id"])
   227	        status = (plan["attrs"].get("status") or "").lower()
   228	        if need is None:
   229	            continue
   230	        if "arrived" in status:  # at the port, not in stock yet: needs collecting
   231	            need.supply.append(
   232	                {
   233	                    "kind": "at_port",
   234	                    "quantity": plan["attrs"].get("quantity"),
   235	                    "reference": plan["reference"],
   236	                    "note": plan["attrs"].get("comment"),
   237	                    "supplier_id": plan["supplier_id"],
   238	                }
   239	            )
   240	        elif launch and plan["attrs"].get("eta") and plan["attrs"]["eta"] > launch:
   241	            need.supply.append(
   242	                {
   243	                    "kind": "after_launch",
   244	                    "quantity": plan["attrs"].get("quantity"),
   245	                    "reference": plan["reference"],
   246	                    "eta": plan["attrs"]["eta"],
   247	                    "supplier_id": plan["supplier_id"],
   248	                }
   249	            )
   250	    for reading in by_kind.get("reading", []):
   251	        if reading["attrs"].get("doc_type") != "offer":
   252	            continue
   253	        for line in (
   254	            r for r in by_kind.get("doc_line", []) if r["doc_path"] == reading["doc_path"]
   255	        ):
   256	            need = needs.get(line["material_id"])
   257	            final = line["attrs"]["final"]
   258	            quantity = next(
   259	                (
   260	                    final[k]
   261	                    for k in (
   262	                        "quantity_confirmed",
   263	                        "quantity_ordered",
   264	                        "quantity_shipped",
   265	                        "quantity_delivered",
   266	                    )
   267	                    if final.get(k)
   268	                ),
   269	                None,
   270	            )
   271	            if need is not None and quantity:
   272	                need.supply.append(
   273	                    {
   274	                        "kind": "offer",
   275	                        "quantity": quantity,
   276	                        "document": reading["doc_path"],
   277	                        "red_flags": reading["attrs"].get("red_flags", [])[:2],
   278	                        # 'loaded within 4 h of your order' + 'about 9 hours driving'
   279	                        "lead_texts": [
   280	                            v["raw"] for v in line["attrs"]["values"] if v["field"] == "lead_time"
   281	                        ]
   282	                        + [
   283	                            s["text_en"]
   284	                            for s in reading["attrs"].get("statements", [])
   285	                            if s.get("topic") == "shipment"
   286	                        ],
   287	                    }
   288	                )

   290	    parts = sorted(needs.values(), key=lambda p: -p.gap)
   291	    result = Shortfall(editions, parts, excluded)
   292	    _add_timing(result, by_kind, launch)
   293	    return result
   294	
   295	
   296	def _add_timing(result: Shortfall, by_kind: dict[str, list[dict]], launch: str | None) -> None:
   297	    """
   298	    When each part runs dry at the packing rate, and which fixes can arrive before then.
   299	
   300	    'Now' is the time of the newest stock or packed count. A fix's act-by time is when it must be
   301	    ordered or decided so it lands before the line runs dry.
   302	    """
   303	    windows = shift_windows([s["attrs"] for s in by_kind.get("plan_shift", [])], launch)
   304	    stamps = [
   305	        parse_moment(r["as_of"])
   306	        for kind in ("stock_count", "packed_count")
   307	        for r in by_kind.get(kind, [])
   308	        if r["as_of"]
   309	    ]
   310	    now = max((s for s in stamps if s), default=None)
   311	    if not windows or now is None:
   312	        return
   313	    result.now = now
   314	    result.packing_ends = windows[-1][1]
   315	    result.hours_left = (
   316	        sum(max((end - max(start, now)).total_seconds(), 0) for start, end in windows) / 3600
   317	    )
   318	    rates = {e.product: e.rate_per_hour for e in result.editions}
   319	    for need in result.parts:
   320	        rate = sum((rates.get(e) or 0) * q for e, q in need.per_copy.items())
   321	        need.rate_per_hour = rate or None
   322	        if rate:
   323	            need.runs_dry = runs_dry(windows, now, need.usable / rate)
   324	        deadline = need.runs_dry or result.packing_ends
   325	        if not need.gap:
   326	            continue
   327	        for supply in need.supply:
   328	            if supply["kind"] == "at_port":
   329	                need.fixes.append(
   330	                    {
   331	                        "kind": "collect",
   332	                        "quantity": min(supply["quantity"] or 0, need.gap),
   333	                        "available": supply["quantity"],
   334	                        "act_by": deadline,
   335	                        "arrives": None,
   336	                        "in_time": True,
   337	                        "reference": supply.get("reference"),
   338	                        "assumption": "collected and unloaded before the line runs dry",
   339	                    }
   340	                )
   341	            elif supply["kind"] == "offer":
   342	                lead = lead_hours(supply.get("lead_texts", []))
   343	                arrives = now + timedelta(hours=lead) if lead is not None else None
   344	                in_time = arrives is not None and arrives <= result.packing_ends
   345	                need.fixes.append(
   346	                    {
   347	                        "kind": "order",
   348	                        "quantity": min(supply["quantity"], need.gap),
   349	                        "available": supply["quantity"],
   350	                        "lead_hours": lead,
   351	                        "act_by": deadline - timedelta(hours=lead) if lead is not None else None,
   352	                        "arrives": arrives,
   353	                        "in_time": in_time,
   354	                        "document": supply.get("document"),
   355	                    }
   356	                )
   357	        for deduction in need.deductions:
   358	            if deduction.reason == "failed inspection":
   359	                need.fixes.append(
   360	                    {
   361	                        "kind": "concession",
   362	                        "quantity": min(deduction.units, need.gap),
   363	                        "available": deduction.units,
   364	                        "act_by": deadline,

   366	                        "in_time": True,

     1	"""
     2	When does a part run out, and by when must someone act?
     3	
     4	Packing time comes from the launch plan's shift table ('Saturday 06:00–22:00'), placed on the
     5	days before launch. 'Now' is the time of the newest stock figures, not the machine clock, so the
     6	answer is the same every time the same data is read. All times are the DC's clock as written.
     7	"""
     8	
     9	import re
    10	from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta
    11	
    12	_TIMES = re.compile(r"(\d{1,2}):(\d{2})\s*[–—-]\s*(\d{1,2}):(\d{2})")
    13	_HOURS = re.compile(r"(\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?)\s*(?:h\b|hrs?\b|hours?\b|godz)", re.I)
    14	WEEKDAYS = ["monday", "tuesday", "wednesday", "thursday", "friday", "saturday", "sunday"]
    15	
    16	
    17	def parse_moment(value: str | None) -> datetime | None:
    18	    """An ISO timestamp from the records (always UTC 'Z' form) as a naive datetime."""
    19	    if not value:
    20	        return None
    21	    try:
    22	        return datetime.fromisoformat(value.replace("Z", "")).replace(tzinfo=None)
    23	    except ValueError:
    24	        return None
    25	
    26	
    27	def shift_windows(shifts: list[dict], launch_date: str | None) -> list[tuple[datetime, datetime]]:
    28	    """
    29	    Packing windows from rows like {'day': 'Saturday', 'shift': '06:00–22:00'}: each weekday is
    30	    placed on its date within the 7 days up to and including launch day.
    31	    """
    32	    if not launch_date:
    33	        return []
    34	    launch = date.fromisoformat(launch_date)
    35	    windows = []
    36	    for shift in shifts:
    37	        day = (shift.get("day") or "").strip().lower()
    38	        match = _TIMES.search(shift.get("shift") or "")
    39	        if day not in WEEKDAYS or not match:
    40	            continue
    41	        offset = (launch.weekday() - WEEKDAYS.index(day)) % 7
    42	        on = launch - timedelta(days=offset)
    43	        h1, m1, h2, m2 = map(int, match.groups())
    44	        start = datetime(on.year, on.month, on.day, h1, m1)
    45	        end = datetime(on.year, on.month, on.day, h2, m2)
    46	        windows.append((start, end))
    47	    return sorted(windows)
    48	
    49	
    50	def hours_left(windows: list[tuple[datetime, datetime]], now: datetime) -> float:
    51	    return sum(max((end - max(start, now)).total_seconds(), 0) for start, end in windows) / 3600
    52	
    53	
    54	def runs_dry(
    55	    windows: list[tuple[datetime, datetime]], now: datetime, packing_hours: float

    12	_TIMES = re.compile(r"(\d{1,2}):(\d{2})\s*[–—-]\s*(\d{1,2}):(\d{2})")
    13	_HOURS = re.compile(r"(\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?)\s*(?:h\b|hrs?\b|hours?\b|godz)", re.I)
    14	WEEKDAYS = ["monday", "tuesday", "wednesday", "thursday", "friday", "saturday", "sunday"]

    17	def parse_moment(value: str | None) -> datetime | None:
    18	    """An ISO timestamp from the records (always UTC 'Z' form) as a naive datetime."""
    19	    if not value:
    20	        return None
    21	    try:

    23	    except ValueError:

    27	def shift_windows(shifts: list[dict], launch_date: str | None) -> list[tuple[datetime, datetime]]:
    28	    """

    30	    placed on its date within the 7 days up to and including launch day.
    31	    """
    32	    if not launch_date:
    33	        return []
    34	    launch = date.fromisoformat(launch_date)
    35	    windows = []
    36	    for shift in shifts:
    37	        day = (shift.get("day") or "").strip().lower()
    38	        match = _TIMES.search(shift.get("shift") or "")

    42	        on = launch - timedelta(days=offset)
    43	        h1, m1, h2, m2 = map(int, match.groups())
    44	        start = datetime(on.year, on.month, on.day, h1, m1)
    45	        end = datetime(on.year, on.month, on.day, h2, m2)

"""

"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd

from ask_soony.verifier.linker.adapters import ADAPTERS, PROFILE_KINDS, Context

class Graph:
    sources: pd.DataFrame  # path, kind, sha256, adapter, records, error

    links: pd.DataFrame
    issues: pd.DataFrame
    coverage: pd.DataFrame

def _run(source: Source, ctx: Context) -> tuple[list[dict], dict]:

        for reading_id, doc_id in lookup.doc_of.items():

    for reading_id, doc_id in lookup.doc_of.items():

                    + (f"; balance expected {expected[-1]}" if expected else "")
                )

                    _issue(
                        "plan_vs_paper",
                        "conflict",
                        plan["record_id"],
                        "Launch plan expects more than the supplier shipped",
                        reading["record_id"],

# Image recognizer (discovery run)

Reads every document (scans, photos, PDFs) with one OpenAI vision call each (`OPENAI_API_KEY` from `.env`). Images are resized and PDF pages without a text layer are rendered to images by the shared `ask_soony.extract`; the answer is forced into the JSON schema in `schema.py`. The goal is to see what the documents say and what kinds of errors keep coming up.

```bash
uv run python -m ask_soony.verifier.image_recognizer                       # all ~277 documents, resumable
uv run python -m ask_soony.verifier.image_recognizer --only WZ-261116-473   # one document
uv run python -m ask_soony.verifier.image_recognizer --images-only --limit 5
```

Options: `--model` (default `gpt-5.4-mini`), `--effort` (default `medium`), `--concurrency` (default 4), `--force` (read again).

## Output: `data/store/image_recognizer/` (gitignored, confidential)

One folder per document, `<path>__<sha12>/`:

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `verdict.json` | Everything on the paper as values: raw text **and** a plain `number` (`80.000` → 80000), printed/handwritten/stamped, crossed out, legible. Plus references, statements, `decisions` (inspection pass/fail, approvals), corrections, and the verdict (status, red flags, observations) |
| `meta.json` | Checksum, model, time, token usage, status, error |

Plus `index.jsonl` (one line per document read) and `run_summary.json` (counts by type, verdict and status, plus errors).

## Behaviour

- **Resumable:** results are keyed by file checksum. Stop any time, and the next run skips what's done. A changed file is read again.
- **Isolated:** one call, no tools; the prompt treats document text as data.
- **Retries:** 2 retries for API or process errors. Refusals and schema failures aren't retried; they're logged and skipped.

"""
Readings (M3): what the image recognizer read from each document, as linker records.

One 'reading' record per document (keys from the references inside it) and one 'doc_line' record
per line on it (part and values). Fixes for known reader errors are applied here, on load:
- counts are re-parsed from the raw text ('19.000' is 19000, see normalize.count_number)
- corrections are derived from the values (crossed out or handwritten), not taken from the
  reader's own list, which mostly holds signatures and stamps
- supplier part numbers are mapped to the buyer's (map_supplier_part_numbers)

The raw text of every value is kept next to the number, so nothing the reader saw is lost.
"""

import hashlib
import json
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

from ask_soony.verifier.linker.normalize import clean, count_number
from ask_soony.verifier.linker.records import make_record

REFERENCE_KEYS = {
    "po_number": "po_numbers",
    "delivery_note": "delivery_note",
    "air_waybill": "reference",
    "container": "reference",
    "batch": "batch",
    "goods_receipt": "batch",  # a goods receipt number is the batch number
}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ReadingSource:
    """Where a reading came from, shaped like a discovered Source for make_record."""

    path: str
    sha256: str


def _references(verdict: dict) -> dict:
    keys: dict = {"po_numbers": []}
    for ref in verdict.get("references") or []:
        column = REFERENCE_KEYS.get(ref.get("type"))
        value = clean(ref.get("value"))
        if column is None or value is None:
            continue
        if column == "po_numbers":
            if value not in keys["po_numbers"]:
                keys["po_numbers"].append(value)
        else:
            keys.setdefault(column, value)
    return keys


def _value(raw: dict) -> dict:
    field = raw.get("field")
    return {
        "field": field if field != "other" else f"other:{raw.get('field_label') or '?'}",
        "raw": raw.get("value"),
        "number": count_number(field, raw.get("value"), raw.get("number")),
        "unit": raw.get("unit"),
        "written": raw.get("written"),
        "crossed_out": bool(raw.get("crossed_out")),
        "legible": raw.get("legible"),
    }


def final_values(values: list[dict]) -> dict:
    """Per field, the value that stands: not crossed out; handwritten beats printed."""
    standing: dict = {}
    for value in values:
        if value["crossed_out"]:
            continue
        current = standing.get(value["field"])
        if current is None or (
            value["written"] == "handwritten" and current["written"] != "handwritten"
        ):
            standing[value["field"]] = value
    return standing


def _current_readings(readings_dir: Path, current_sha: dict[str, str]) -> list[Path]:
    """
    One reading per document. A document read twice (its file changed in between) keeps only
    the reading of its current version; with no current reading, the old ones stay, marked stale.
